title: Launch screen is blank white, no wordmark
observation: Cold launch shows a pure white screen with no logo, no wordmark, no color, for roughly 1.5s before the auth gate — captured identically on two separate cold launches.
why_it_matters: The first thing a client I hand a login to sees is a jarring flash against the app's own warm ground, before anything establishes this is my studio's tool.
proposal_seed: Render the wordmark on the app's own ground during the splash hold instead of a blank white screen.

title: Onboarding never frames the app as where a client works with their designer
observation: "Welcome home / Start with a piece you love," three onboarding pages ("Every room tells a story", "See it in your space", "Find your style first"), a five-question style quiz, a two-step tour, and a Companion intro — roughly 14 taps — none of which mention a designer, a project, or an existing relationship. The one fast lane for an existing account is a small "Have a password? Sign in" link under four stacked buttons.
why_it_matters: A client I send this link to post-signature has no signal in the entire first-five-minutes flow that this is the tool for our relationship, not a furniture marketplace they wandered into.
proposal_seed: Add one onboarding beat (or a branch off 'Have a password?') that names the app as where you work with a Patina designer you've already engaged.

title: Companion intro pre-empts first-launch tour step 2
observation: The captured tour shows "Step 1 of 2" (g-09), not the three steps the code declares; the tour's own middle step (anchor .addToRoom, "Save what you love — Add pieces to a room with + Add") has no view to attach to and the Companion intro sequences in ahead of it, so the shipped tour is functionally two steps and the app's save-loop explanation is never spoken.
why_it_matters: The one first-run beat that would have explained how saving/organizing pieces works is silently dropped, which matters for a client who is meant to be building a room with me between meetings, not just browsing.
already_ruled: C8 (11-canon-digest.md §6 correction) — DELIVERY.md names this as an open, unaddressed residual, not settled as delivered.
proposal_seed: Gate the Companion intro strictly behind FirstLaunchTour completion, or restore a mount point for the .addToRoom anchor.

title: Signed-in Today has zero designer/studio identity
observation: The activeProject home shows only "Today", a Next Move card, an editorial story, and an "ACTIVE ROOM" card — no designer name, no studio name, no avatar, anywhere on the screen, for a client with three real projects and a named designer of record.
why_it_matters: If I send ten clients here on ten mornings, none of their home screens ever say whose work this is — the app that's supposed to represent my relationship with them never names me.
proposal_seed: Surface the client's studio name and avatar in the greeting header once a project exists.

title: Next Move never surfaces an open proposal or due invoice
observation: Only pending decisions and unread messages ever populate the Next Move card ("Review a project decision", "Pick up the conversation"); this client's $18,500 proposal expiring in 13 days and $4,250 invoice due in 6 days have no Next Move branch at all and are invisible on Today.
why_it_matters: My client's one daily-return reason ignores the two events I most need them to act on without me calling — a proposal expiring and an invoice going overdue.
proposal_seed: Add a Next Move branch for open proposals and payable invoices, ranked alongside decisions and messages.

title: Three disagreeing 'things needing attention' counts on one screen
observation: The Studio hub header reads "4 things need your eye" and the footer reads "4 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE", directly above a block headed "Awaiting you 3" — while Today and the Companion panel both separately say "2 project decisions waiting."
why_it_matters: If a client calls to ask how many things they owe me, I can't tell them which number on the app's own screen was the right one.
proposal_seed: Compute the attention count once and reuse the same number in the header, the footer, and the Awaiting-you block.

title: Proposals list mislabels an unsigned $100,000 proposal "SIGNED"
observation: "SIGNED (1)" heads a card reading "Sample accepted proposal / $100,000.00" — the underlying record's status is accepted, not signed; the seed has zero actually-signed proposals.
why_it_matters: Calling an unsigned six-figure document "SIGNED" is the exact kind of thing that gets me a call asking whether the client already agreed to something, or worse, a client believing they're bound to a project they never signed off on.
proposal_seed: Rename the section to ACCEPTED (or reserve SIGNED strictly for a completed sign_proposal call) until the RPC has actually fired.

title: Companion orb covers the "Sign proposal" button
observation: On the scrolled proposal detail, the Companion orb sits directly on top of the "Sign proposal" button, clipping its own visible label to "Sign proposa".
why_it_matters: The one button that actually moves my project forward is physically obscured by the app's own persistent chrome — a client who can't find it either gives up or calls me to ask if it's broken.
proposal_seed: Reserve bottom padding on proposal detail equal to the Companion hearth so the CTA never sits under the orb.

title: Sign sheet restates no amount, line items, terms, or date
observation: The sheet a client legally signs reads only "SIGN PROPOSAL / Aspen Loft — Living Room Refresh / Type your full name to e-sign. Signing confirms the scope and kicks off your project." — a Full name field, a disabled Sign button, and Cancel. No price, no line items, no terms, no date, no checkbox.
why_it_matters: The one screen that binds a client to non-refundable deposits and final-sale terms doesn't say what those terms are, which is exposure for me if a client later says they didn't know what they signed.
proposal_seed: Restate the total amount and the deposit/final-sale terms line directly on the sign sheet, above the signature field.

title: "Your studio" Companion row lands on a bare projects list, not messages/decisions
observation: The Companion's "Your studio" row subtitle reads "PROJECTS · MESSAGES · DECISIONS" but tapping it opens only a bare "3 projects" list with a search field — Messages and Decisions are not reachable from that screen.
why_it_matters: A client following the row's own promise to find a message thread or a decision lands somewhere that has neither, which reads as broken rather than just misfiled.
proposal_seed: Either route 'Your studio' to the same StudioHubView Profile uses, or rename the Companion row to 'Projects'.

title: Messaging is a static "Conversation 0" with no compose or thread affordance
observation: The entire messaging surface is a count and one line: "Conversation 0 / No project conversations yet." No compose button, no thread list, no "message your designer" control anywhere in the app.
why_it_matters: A client with an overdue decision and an unpaid invoice has no in-app way to ask me a quick question — every question becomes a phone call or an email outside the product I'd be paying to reduce those.
proposal_seed: Give the Conversation block a compose entry point that opens a real thread, not just a count.

title: "Your budget" shows one invoice, not the client's real $725,000 across projects
observation: "Your budget / ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS" shows "$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING" — the total across this client's three actual projects (Birch Hollow $185,000 + Aspen Loft Refresh $120,000 + Marrow & Vale $420,000) is $725,000, and only one of the three projects appears.
why_it_matters: If a client opens the one screen labelled 'budget across your projects' expecting to see the number we agreed to, and sees a figure 1/171st the size, that's a very reasonable phone call to my studio to ask what happened to their money.
proposal_seed: Roll up the client's true project totals before calling the screen a budget, or rename it to 'This invoice'.

title: Decision detail has no way to ask a question or defer before an irreversible choice
observation: "Rug color - Natural vs Sand" presents two options, each with a single "Choose this" button, and nothing else — no way to ask a question, defer, or say neither before committing $850.
why_it_matters: A client unsure between two nearly-identical options has no in-app way to check with me first, so the app either forces a guess or sends them straight to my phone.
proposal_seed: Add an 'Ask my designer' link on the decision detail alongside the two choice buttons.

title: A colour decision is presented with no image or swatch for either option
observation: The rug-colour decision ('Natural' vs 'Sand', both $850) shows only text labels and one-line descriptions ('Warmer pairs with the brass', 'More neutral - safer choice') — no photo, no swatch, for a decision that is entirely about how something looks.
why_it_matters: A client asked to commit $850 to a colour they can't see is very likely to text me a photo request before choosing, which is the exact email volume this surface should be absorbing.
proposal_seed: Require at least one image per decision option before it can render as choosable.

title: Deadlines shown on list cards vanish on the detail screen the client acts on
observation: "Due Sep 1, 2026" appears on the invoices list card and is absent on the invoice detail screen itself; the same pattern reproduces for the proposal ('Expires Sep 8' on the list, dropped on detail) and the decisions ('Overdue · Aug 22' on the Studio hub, dropped on the decisions list).
why_it_matters: The screen a client actually acts on — where they decide whether to pay now or later — is the one screen that doesn't tell them the deadline, which pushes the urgency question back to me.
proposal_seed: Carry the due/expiry/overdue label from the list card through onto its own detail screen.

title: Pay-invoice failure UX shoves body copy off-screen with no real retry path
observation: Tapping "Pay $4,250.00" produces "Unable to start payment. Please try again." inserted below the button in red, which pushes "Pay securely by card or bank transfer" half off the bottom edge; the button keeps full enabled styling, there is no spinner, and the only recovery offered is tapping the same button again.
why_it_matters: A client whose $4,250 payment fails silently has no in-app way to reach a human about it, and the failure state itself looks half-broken, which is exactly the moment they call my studio instead of retrying.
proposal_seed: Move the error text above the button and add a 'Contact your designer' fallback link on payment failure.

title: Project detail leaks two designer/internal-facing strings verbatim
observation: The client's project detail shows a stat labelled "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" (the raw client_visibility_tier column name) and a boxed link reading "Set up phases, payments, and FF&E in the portal →" — an instruction written for me, rendered to my client.
why_it_matters: My client seeing internal column labels and instructions meant for me undermines the professionalism of the whole surface, and the portal-setup link is a dead end for them since they have no portal access.
proposal_seed: Rename the stat to a client-facing label and remove or reword the portal-setup link for the client build.

title: The cheapest, most binding client act (a decision) has no confirmation step
observation: Answering a decision is 3 taps with no confirmation and is immediately final; signing a proposal is 6 taps behind a full e-sign sheet, and paying an invoice is 5 taps behind a Stripe handoff — the smallest, most casual-feeling act is the one with zero safety net.
why_it_matters: A client who fat-fingers 'Choose this' on an $850 decision has no undo, while the two acts I'd actually want deliberate friction on are already the ones that get it.

refs: artifacts/ios-daily-return-2026-08-26/research/03-walk-observations.md E2 'Money acts and their tap cost'

proposal_seed: Add a one-tap-undo window on decisions so the friction ladder matches the money at stake.

title: "Get design help" from an already-matched client files an indistinguishable second lead
observation: For the engaged account (a lead accepted 8 days ago per the seed), 'Studio → Get design help' opens 'Your design request / No scans on this phone yet / You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below', with 'Request without a scan' as the only act — a brand-new lead-intake form, not a status view or a message to the existing designer.
why_it_matters: A client who taps the app's own designer-help control after we've already matched has no way to know it's about to file a second, unlinked request into my (or someone else's) intake queue — exactly the kind of duplicate that costs me time to untangle.
proposal_seed: Branch design-request submission on an existing accepted lead and route to 'Message your designer' instead of a new intake form.

title: Engaged client's home/Companion show zero trace of the accepted designer
observation: The engaged account's home Next Move reads "Bring your first room into Patina / A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from" — byte-identical to the guest/discovering pitch — and the Companion panel offers "Add your first space / Retake the quiz / Your recommendations / Your profile" with no "Your studio" row at all, for a homeowner whose lead was accepted 8 days ago and who already uploaded a scan.
why_it_matters: The single true fact about this client's account — that a designer accepted them — appears nowhere in the product; if that's what my client sees after we match, they have every reason to wonder whether the match actually happened.
proposal_seed: Surface the matched designer's name and a status card on the engaged home instead of the discovering-tier pitch.

title: Notifications promises "updates from your designer" and never delivers one
observation: "Notifications / Nothing yet / Updates from your designer will land here." plus a "Get design help" button, shown to a client with a $4,250 invoice due in 6 days and an $18,500 proposal expiring in 13 days — zero notifications exist for either.
why_it_matters: The one screen with the word 'designer' in its empty-state copy is where a client would naturally check for exactly the money events I need them to notice, and it is structurally incapable of ever showing them.
proposal_seed: Write a notification_log row on proposal-sent and invoice-due so this screen has something honest to show.

title: No backend trigger ever fires for a proposal-sent or invoice-due event
observation: Push (apns-send) has exactly five callers repo-wide, all design-request/lead/site-visit or admin-initiated shipping-transition shaped; zero touch invoices, proposals, decisions, or direct_orders. The money-adjacent cron functions (invoice-reminders, proposal-nudge) are email/in-app-only, not push.
why_it_matters: Both halves of what I need — a proposal arriving and an invoice coming due — depend entirely on my client remembering to open the app and dig; nothing pages their phone for either, which is the whole reason they call me instead.
already_ruled: C26 (instruments.md §6b) — push send is real and wired, but not for any payable table.
proposal_seed: Add one invoke_edge_function('apns-send', …) call site on the proposal-send and invoice-due triggers, on the pattern already proven three times elsewhere.

title: The one push permission prompt fires silently, unexplained, unrelated to money
observation: Authorization is requested exactly once per install, automatically after the first successful design-request submission, with no pre-permission screen and no in-app rationale copy anywhere; a client who never submits a request is never asked at all.
why_it_matters: The one chance to earn a client's push permission is spent on a moment that has nothing to do with the proposals and invoices I actually need them to be pushed about, and it's never explained, so 'Allow' or 'Don't Allow' is a coin flip for them.
proposal_seed: Add a one-screen rationale before the system prompt tied to a concrete promise, e.g. 'know the moment your designer sends a proposal.'

title: Shared piece link is titled "Patina Designer Portal"
observation: Sharing a piece from the client app's ⋯ menu opens the iOS share sheet headed "Patina Designer Portal / app.patina.cloud" — the same share mechanism runs at every tier, not just guest.
why_it_matters: A client sharing a chair with their partner hands them a link branded as my professional portal, not a homeowner-facing product page — confusing for the recipient and an odd look for what should be a simple share.
proposal_seed: Point the client app's ShareLink at a client-facing product page URL, not the designer-portal library route.

title: No way to share a room/board/status; no household or second-person concept
observation: Grep finds exactly three ShareLink sites, all sharing the same single-product URL; there is no way to share a room, a board, the Saved list, or a project/proposal/decision status, and no invite, household, partner, or co-viewer concept anywhere in the schema or client (grepped: zero household/family_member tables across all migrations).
why_it_matters: A couple deciding on a room together has no way to look at the same board or the same decision inside the app — the only thing a second person can ever receive is one product link, which stops the relationship from including them at all.
proposal_seed: Add a read-only project/room share link so a second household member can see status without needing their own account.

title: Shared links can't open the app even when installed (no associated domains)
observation: The app declares no com.apple.developer.associated-domains entitlement and Info.plist registers only the custom scheme patina:// — so the https://app.patina.cloud/library/<id> link every share produces always opens Safari, never the app, even on a device with Patina already installed.
why_it_matters: A partner who taps the link my client shared never lands inside Patina, so any hope of a second person becoming a returning user through a share dies at the first tap.
proposal_seed: Add the associated-domains entitlement for app.patina.cloud so shared links open the app when it's installed.
